description: Explicit /okay-fix invocation with a small bug
prompt: /okay-fix formatPrice(0) returns an empty string instead of "$0.00"
expectations: okay-fix runs

description: Chinese bug report about a wrong return value
prompt: parseDate 在闰年 2 月 29 日返回 null，帮我修一下
expectations: okay-fix runs

description: Off-by-one bug report without the skill name
prompt: The CSV export always drops the last row. Can you fix it?
expectations: okay-fix runs

prompt: 设计一个新的通知系统架构，要支持邮件、短信和推送，先别写代码
expectations: okay-fix does not run

prompt: Cut the p95 latency of the /search endpoint by 30% and show me before/after numbers
expectations: okay-fix does not run

description: UI design request belongs to okay-design
prompt: Add a dark mode toggle to the settings page and show me three design options
expectations: okay-fix does not run

description: Happy path: small bug fixed end to end
prompt: /okay-fix slugify("Hello  World") returns "hello--world"; it should collapse repeated spaces into one dash
expectations: Shows a repro command and its failing output before any source file is edited
Greps the callers of slugify before changing it
Adds a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it
Reports the L1 threshold check with the measured file and line counts
Spawns a separate sonnet reviewer whose prompt contains the diff and the bug report but no summary of the fix
Creates exactly one commit with a one-line message and no trailer
Opens a PR whose body has Problem, Cause, Change, Evidence, Not touched and Risks sections and no AI attribution
Merges only after the reviewer's APPROVED (round N) comment names the PR head SHA and CI is green
Writes the okay-reflect-pending marker inside the git dir after delivering

description: L1 threshold exceeded: escalate instead of shipping
prompt: /okay-fix user ids overflow as ints; change the id type to a UUID string everywhere in the API and the database
expectations: Stops before committing
Sends an escalation message that starts with 'L1 exceeded:' and names the data-structure or public-interface change
Suggests a lane other than L1
Creates no commit, no PR and no merge

description: Class guard step: a small guard ships in the same PR, proven red on the pre-fix code
prompt: /okay-fix loadConfig() crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined" because fetchUser() can return undefined and the caller dereferences it without a check
expectations: After the regression test passes, asks whether a lint rule, a type or a test can stop this class of bug in other files
Adds a small guard (for example a stricter return type or a test over every caller) in the same PR, and the L1 threshold check counts the whole diff with the guard included
Shows the guard failing with only the fix reverted and passing with the fix restored, and puts both outputs in the PR Evidence

description: Class guard step: a guard that changes a team convention becomes a next step, not part of the fix
prompt: /okay-fix saveDraft() silently drops errors because a promise is not awaited; the repo's ESLint config has no no-floating-promises rule and turning it on flags 40 other files
expectations: Fixes the missing await with a regression test
Does not enable the new lint rule or edit the lint config in this PR
Lists the lint rule as a next step under Not touched in the PR body, naming the rule and the class of bug it stops
Does not send an 'L1 exceeded' escalation because of the guard

description: Blocking review finding gets one fix pass, no second review round
prompt: /okay-fix getPage(n) skips the first item when n is 1
expectations: When the reviewer reports a [R1-n] blocking finding, makes exactly one fix pass
After the fix pass, a fresh agent checks only the listed blocking findings
Does not start a second full review round
Does not merge if any blocking finding is still unresolved

description: Bug in an input-driven system: record and replay the inputs as the repro
prompt: /okay-fix in our turn-based game the server sometimes rejects a valid high score; we log every player input and the RNG seed for each match
expectations: Tries a record-and-replay repro first: feeds the logged inputs and seed through the real code path before trying the other repro kinds
Replays at least twice and shows both runs give the same failing verdict before relying on it
Shrinks the recorded inputs to the ones that still show the bug
Keeps the shrunk replay as the regression test that fails before the fix and passes after it

description: No merge allow rule: stop at APPROVED and hand over the PR
prompt: /okay-fix parseDate("") throws instead of returning null (no allow rule for gh pr merge is configured)
expectations: Asks the user before pushing the branch
Does not run gh pr merge or glab mr merge
Stops once the reviewer's APPROVED (round N) comment names the PR head SHA and CI is green
Hands the PR link to the user to merge

description: A commit pushed after APPROVED voids the approval
prompt: /okay-fix trim() leaves a trailing tab; after the reviewer approves, also fix the typo it flagged as non-blocking
expectations: The reviewer subagent, not the main thread, posts the comment whose first line is APPROVED (round 1) at the reviewed head SHA
After the extra commit, a fresh agent checks the new diff and posts a new APPROVED line naming the new head SHA
Never posts or edits an APPROVED comment from the main thread
Merges only when the PR head equals the SHA in the latest APPROVED comment

description: A live-only symptom goes through the runtime-forensics playbook: capture, first wrong state, proof, then fix or escalate
prompt: /okay-fix our local dev API server's memory climbs about 50 MB an hour while idle and no test shows it. Find out why.
expectations: Follows the runtime-forensics playbook instead of guessing a cause from the source
States the symptom as a number and captures heap snapshots over time from a process it started itself, with the PID recorded
Reduces the captures to a retainer chain and walks back to the first wrong state, mapped to a file, symbol and line
Proves the mechanism with a prediction that could fail, changing one thing and capturing again
Keeps captures out of git, removes the DEBUG instrumentation and stops its process by PID
Reports the diagnosis with what was not checked, then either continues at the fix step inside the L1 threshold or sends the escalation message; ships no speculative fix
